title: Train, Evaluate and Persist Weights
summary: Review minibatch updates, dropout modes and restored-state prediction checks.

steps.title: Implement the minibatch forward, backward and optimizer-step loop

blocks.text: Every minibatch in each declared epoch needs the intended current-gradient update and enough loss evidence to interpret partial batches.

Inside each epoch, iterate for features, targets in loader. Compute model(features) and loss_fn(predictions, targets). For each minibatch, call optimizer.zero_grad(), loss.backward() and optimizer.step(). Collect scalar loss.item() evidence with batch counts so an incomplete batch is represented correctly in the epoch summary.

Assert the valid, boundary and failure predicates; a false predicate raises AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution. In a plain-SGD fixture, retain pre-step parameters and check parameter_after − parameter_before against −learning_rate × current_gradient under tolerance.

blocks.code:
import torch
from torch import nn
from torch.utils.data import TensorDataset, DataLoader
features = torch.arange(5, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(5, 1)
targets = features.clone()
loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(features, targets), batch_size=2,
                    shuffle=False, drop_last=False)
model = nn.Linear(1, 1, bias=False)
with torch.no_grad():
    model.weight.fill_(2.)
learning_rate = 0.1
rtol, atol = 1e-5, 1e-6
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate,
                            momentum=0, weight_decay=0)
criterion = nn.MSELoss(reduction="mean")
epoch_records = []
step_checks = []
for epoch in range(1):
    loss_count_pairs = []
    for batch_features, batch_targets in loader:
        batch_count = len(batch_features)
        assert batch_count == len(batch_targets)
        assert torch.equal(batch_features, batch_targets)
        parameter_before = model.weight.detach().clone()
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        outputs = model(batch_features)
        loss = criterion(outputs, batch_targets)
        loss.backward()
        current_gradient = model.weight.grad.detach().clone()
        optimizer.step()
        parameter_after = model.weight.detach().clone()
        change_ok = torch.allclose(parameter_after - parameter_before,
                                   -learning_rate * current_gradient,
                                   rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
        assert change_ok
        step_checks.append((parameter_before, current_gradient, parameter_after, change_ok))
        loss_count_pairs.append((loss.item(), batch_count))
    assert [count for scalar_loss, count in loss_count_pairs] == [2, 2, 1]
    epoch_records.append(loss_count_pairs)

annotations.text: Each minibatch gets its own current-gradient update; the final loss is paired with count 1, not the configured maximum 2.

The loop calls zero_grad only before the epoch; each minibatch then calls backward and step.
The loop records every batch count as configured batch_size=2, including the retained final one-observation batch.
Each step is checked only for a nonzero parameter change, with no comparison to −learning_rate × current_gradient.

steps.title: Apply correct neural-network training and evaluation modes

blocks.text: Validation needs two controls: layer behavior and gradient recording. Neither control replaces the other.

model.train() selects training behavior; model.eval() selects validation behavior for relevant layers such as dropout and batch normalization. Use with torch.no_grad(): around validation prediction to disable gradient-graph recording. eval changes layer behavior, while no_grad changes recording.

left.code:
import torch
from torch import nn
layer = nn.Dropout(p=0.5)
inputs = torch.tensor([1., 2., 3., 4.], requires_grad=True)
layer.train()
training_output = layer(inputs)
with torch.no_grad():
    training_no_grad_output = layer(inputs)
for output in (training_output, training_no_grad_output):
    assert torch.all((output == 0) | (output == 2 * inputs))
assert not training_no_grad_output.requires_grad
# Neither call is required to drop at least one element.

right.code:
layer.eval()
evaluation_output = layer(inputs)
assert torch.equal(evaluation_output, inputs)
# This is the same layer; mode and gradient recording are independent.
layer.train()

blocks.left_label: Training, with and without gradient recording
blocks.takeaway: Training under no_grad still applies dropout; evaluation changes layer behavior independently of gradient recording.

blocks.text: Validation is forward-only: omit optimizer.step() and restore model.train() before the next training pass. Test valid, boundary and failure predicates with assert; false predicates raise AssertionError in ordinary non-optimized execution. Import torch and nn from torch for the supplied nn.Dropout(p=0.5) fixture. Training randomly zeros each element with probability p and scales retained values by 1/(1-p). Evaluation returns x unchanged. Check identity and permitted masking/scaling without requiring every random call to mask an element. no_grad does not select evaluation behavior.

In the supplied dropout fixture, inspect mode and recording context independently. Evaluation behaves as an identity even when recording is enabled. Training can still mask and scale values inside no_grad. Compare the permitted stochastic outcomes rather than demanding a particular random mask. Validation also excludes updates; disabling the graph alone does not describe the whole pass. Restore training mode afterward.
eval does not disable recording; no_grad does not switch dropout behavior. Validation must also exclude parameter updates.

segments.label: Training and validation use two independent controls
segments.summary: Use model.train() before parameter training and model.eval() before validation. These settings change the behavior of layers such as dropout and batch normalization; leaving training behavior active can introduce unwanted variability into validation scores. Separately, wrap validation computation in torch.no_grad() to prevent gradient graph recording. Evaluation mode controls layer behavior, not graph recording. Each training epoch begins by restoring training mode, computing the forward pass and loss, clearing gradients, running backward, and stepping the optimizer. The separate validation block switches to evaluation mode and computes validation loss inside no_grad without updating parameters. Recording both losses keeps the training and validation measurements distinct.

```python
import torch
from torch import nn
layer = nn.Dropout(p=0.5)
layer.train()
train_output = layer(x)
assert ((train_output == 0) | (train_output == 2*x)).all()
# The all-retained boundary 2*x satisfies the same predicate.
layer.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    validation_output = layer(x)
assert torch.equal(validation_output, x)
# No optimizer.step in validation.
layer.train()
assert layer.training
```

The all-retained training result 2*x is rejected because the test requires at least one zero.

steps.title: Save and reload neural-network weights for prediction

blocks.text: Restoring learned state requires a compatible architecture and checks of both parameters and fixed-fixture predictions.

torch.save(model.state_dict(), path) saves learned parameters. Reconstruct the same compatible architecture, read the mapping with torch.load(path, weights_only=True), and apply model.load_state_dict(mapping). Select model.eval() before restored prediction.

Compare original and restored evaluation predictions on the same fixture with explicit numerical tolerances. Assert valid, boundary and failure predicates; false predicates raise AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution. For the specified handle-based path, open with open(path, "wb") to save and open(path, "rb") to load, passing the binary handle to torch.save or torch.load.
Also compare corresponding original and restored state_dict entries to verify preserved parameter state.

left.code:
import torch
from torch import nn
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from pathlib import Path

def compatible_architecture():
    return nn.Linear(2, 1)

model = compatible_architecture()
fixed_input = torch.tensor([[1., 2.], [3., 4.]])
rtol, atol = 1e-5, 1e-6
original_entries = {name: value.detach().clone()
                    for name, value in model.state_dict().items()}
model.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    original_predictions = model(fixed_input).detach().clone()
temporary = TemporaryDirectory()
path = Path(temporary.name) / "weights.pt"
with open(path, "wb") as handle:
    torch.save(model.state_dict(), handle)

right.code:
restored = compatible_architecture()
with open(path, "rb") as handle:
    mapping = torch.load(handle, weights_only=True)
restored.load_state_dict(mapping)
restored_entries = restored.state_dict()
assert original_entries.keys() == restored_entries.keys()
entry_equal = {name: torch.equal(value, restored_entries[name])
               for name, value in original_entries.items()}
assert all(entry_equal.values())
name = next(iter(original_entries))
differing_entry = original_entries[name] + 1
assert not torch.equal(differing_entry, restored_entries[name])
restored.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    restored_predictions = restored(fixed_input)
predictions_match = torch.allclose(original_predictions, restored_predictions,
                                   rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
assert predictions_match
temporary.cleanup()

items.text:
```python
original.eval()
with torch.no_grad(): reference = original(fixture)
with open(path, "wb") as handle:
    torch.save(original.state_dict(), handle)
restored = same_architecture()
with open(path, "rb") as handle:
    mapping = torch.load(handle, weights_only=True)
restored.load_state_dict(mapping)
restored.eval()
for name, value in original.state_dict().items():
    assert torch.allclose(value, restored.state_dict()[name], rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
with torch.no_grad(): prediction = restored(fixture)
assert torch.allclose(prediction, reference, rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
```
